baden-wurttemberg: Southwestern state with the Black Forest, Mercedes and Porsche; capital Stuttgart
bavaria: Largest state, home of Oktoberfest and Neuschwanstein; capital Munich
berlin: City-state and national capital, once divided by a wall
brandenburg: State surrounding the capital; capital Potsdam
bremen: The smallest state: a northern port city-state with famous town musicians
hamburg: Germany's biggest port, a city-state on the Elbe
hesse: Central state with the banking city of Frankfurt; capital Wiesbaden
lower-saxony: Large northwestern state, home of Volkswagen; capital Hanover
mecklenburg-western-pomerania: Baltic coast state of lakes and islands like Rügen; capital Schwerin
north-rhine-westphalia: The most populous state, with Cologne and the Ruhr; capital Düsseldorf
rhineland-palatinate: Wine country along the Rhine and Moselle; capital Mainz
saarland: Small coal-mining state on the French border; capital Saarbrücken
saxony: Eastern state with Dresden and Leipzig
saxony-anhalt: Eastern state with Magdeburg and the Harz mountains' Brocken nearby
schleswig-holstein: Northernmost state between two seas, bordering Denmark; capital Kiel
thuringia: The "green heart" of Germany, with Weimar and Erfurt
